purchaser of the property of the agricultural land bearing survey No.468, Block No.401,

2.1 Advocate Mr.Shaikh, submits that the agricultural land was under the personal occupation and ownership of Amliben widow of Chhitiya Kalia, who had died on 13.03.1978.
Thereafter, the agricultural land was mutated in the name of sole heir Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai Solanki by Revenue Entry No.1885 dated 01.09.1997.

Mr.Shaiksh submits that Bhikhabhai Chittabhai died on 14.08.2003, and therefore, the said agricultural land was mutated in the name of his legal heirs viz.
(i) Madhuben widow of Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai and his four daughters viz. Manjuben, Jashuben,
Bhartiben and Vasantiben by entry no.2230 on 13.09.2023.
Mr.Shaikh submits that the entry was certified by the higher revenue officer and the heirs are recorded being ostensible owners and occupants of the said agricultural land.

Mr.Shaikh submitted that the heirs of deceased Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai is shown as accused No.1 to 5 in the said complaint of respondent No.2.

2.2 Advocate Mr.Shaikh submits that the petitioner had purchased the said land from the heirs of Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai under the registered sale deed dated 17.02.2010 for the consideration of Rs.1,75,000/- duly executed by them in favour of the petitioner and to that effect, revenue entry No.3338 dated 25.02.2010 was effected in the revenue record of the said agricultural land evidencing the sale transaction.
2.3
Advocate Mr.Shaikh submits that the said agricultural land was in personal cultivation and occupation as an independent owner of the petitioner since that date i.e. 17.02.2010.

Thereafter, the petitioner has sold the agricultural land to Sangita Bhikhabhai Khunt, an Advocate and agriculturist by registered sale deed dated 13.09.2012 for Rs.4,50,000/- and the revenue entry No.3539 reflects the said transaction.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4830/2013 ORDER DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined 2.4

Advocate Mr.Shaikh submits that challenge has been given to the complaint as it has been after a considerable long time and inordinate delay has not been explained as the Criminal Complaint No.7 of 2012 was filed on 28.03.2012 by the respondent No.2 against the five heirs of the deceased Bhikhabhai Chhitbhai in the Court of Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Surat for the alleged offence under Sections 406, 420 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code alleging that the deceased Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai had agreed to sell the agricultural land to him in the year 1998 and he had accepted the full amount of consideration and the possession of the agricultural land was given by Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai to the complainant, and for that, possession receipt was executed to power of attorney drawn in favour of Rajivkumar Bharatsinh Chauhan, son of the complainant. Thereafter,
complainant/respondent No.2 had requested the heirs of the deceased Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai to execute the registered sale deed in his favour but they had not NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4830/2013 ORDER DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined agreed to do so.

2.5 Advocate Mr.Shaikh submits that the complainant has alleged that the daughters of the deceased Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai had filed a Regular Civil Suit No.8 of 2004 through the power of attorney Ashokbhai Chandrakant Ramanandi vs State Of Gujarat on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177348021/
2 Harshadbhai Chimanbhai Parmar and the Civil Suit was compromised in Lok Adalat on 30.10.2004 and the power of attorney of the daughters of deceased Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai had waived their rights over the said agricultural land and amount of Rs.1,00,000/- was paid by the respondent No.2 to them, and the possession of the said agricultural land was handed over by the daughters of the deceased of Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai to respondent No.2 on 30.10.2004 and the allegation is that the heirs of deceased Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai in association with the petitioner, had executed sale deed dated 17.02.2010 in favour of the petitioner, and for that, entry No.3338 dated 25.02.2010 was mutated.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4830/2013 ORDER DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined 2.6
Advocate Mr.Shaikh submits that the complainant had preferred RTS Appeal No.136 of 2010 against the said entry in the Court of Deputy Collector, Mandvi, Surat, which is pending.

While on the complaint filed by respondent No.2, the learned Civil Judge, Mangrol passed the order on 05.04.2012 directing the Police Sub Inspector, Kosamba to investigate the said complaint under Section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, and thereupon, Kosamba police has registered the offence under Sections 406, 420, 114 of Indian Penal Code against the petitioner and the heirs of the deceased Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai bearing M case No. 2/2012. 2.7

Advocate Mr.Shaikh submits that after investigation, widow of Bhikhabhai Chitabhai was arrested by the police on 04.02.2013, and she was produced before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Mangrol, and thereafter on 06.12.2013,
the petitioner was released on bail.

He further submits that the petitioner and four daughters of the deceased Bhiikhabhai Chhitabhai were arrested by NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4830/2013 ORDER DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined the police on 26.02.2013.

Thereafter, they moved bail application but their bail application was rejected by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class,
Mangrol, and thereafter, they filed application under Section 439 of the Criminal Procedure Code before the Principal District and Session Judge, Surat, wherein the learned Sessions Judge has released the petitioner and others accused on bail on 05.03.2013 2.8

sentences.text: Advocate Mr.Shaikh submits that the respondent No.2 has stated that in the year 1998 deceased Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai had agreed to sell the agricultural land to the respondent no 2, and the consideration was also accepted by him and the possession was handed over but no action was initiated through the Civil Court against the deceased Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai during his life time upto 14.08.2003 for claiming specific performance of the agreement.
He further submits that the respondent No. 2 had compromised the Civil Suit No. 8 of 2004 in the Lok-Adalat on 30.10.2004.

If that has been the case, then why again on that day, the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4830/2013 ORDER DATED:
19/01/2023 undefined respondent No 2 had again taken possession of the suit land through the compromise executed in the Lok-Adalat from the plaintiffs i.e. daughters of deceased Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai.

Even no action has been initiated by respondent No 2 against the daughters of the deceased Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai, from the date of compromise i.e. 30.10.2004 till the date of filing of the present complaint in the year 2012 for claiming specific performance of the agreement.

2.9. Advocate Mr.Shaikh submits that the FIR against the petitioner is manifestly perverse, unjust and patently illegal resulting into misuse of the process of the Court and thus, has made prayer for quashing and setting aside the Criminal Complaint bearing M Case No.2 of 2012 and order dated 05.04.2012 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Mangrol in Criminal Case No.7 of 2012 against the present petitioner.

sentences.text: Countering the arguments, Mr. N.V. Gandhi, learned advocate for respondent No.2 submits that NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4830/2013 ORDER DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined the complainant had purchased the land from the father of Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai in the year 1998 and Regular Civil Suit No.8 of 2004 was filed by the daughters of Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai through the power of attorney Harshadbhai Chimanbhai Parmar against the complainant and Girishbhai Harijan and the widow of deceased Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai.

3.1 Advocate Mr.Gandhi submits that the defendant No.2 Girishbhai is a mediator in the matter and the case was settled in the Lok-Adalat on 30.10.2004, and accordingly, again the complainant-present respondent gave Rs.1,00,000/- to the plaintiff.

He further submits that actually, it was a family property partition, and defendant No.3- mother was given the ownership of two houses in village Velachha, Taluka Mangrol, Dist.
Surat; while on the disputed property bearing block No.401, right was totally granted to the complainant - present respondent No.2.
3.2
Advocate Mr.Gandhi submits that the settlement was signed by all the parties i.e. NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4830/2013 ORDER DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined

Harshadbhai Chimanbhai Parmar, power of attorney of the sisters, widow of Bhikha Chhitabhai and the mother of the plaintiffs had put her thumb impression before the Court and the learned Civil Judge,
Mangrol had accepted the settlement in the Lok-Adalat, which was drawn in the presence of conciliator.

Mr. Gandhi further submits that the learned Judge while passing the order and accepting the settlement has also referred the names of conciliators, who were Advocate practicing in the Court, and thereafter, decree had been drawn.
Thus, it is stated that the fact was known to all the sisters regarding the partition of the family property.

Therefore, the petitioner cannot be termed as a bonafide purchaser and the petitioner being the bonafide person should have waited for the decision of the Court while petition suggests that he had again sold the property to one Sangitaben,
who is Advocate and agriculturist on 13.09.2012 which would again draw the complainant into more litigation.

Mr. Gandhi submitted that this is no simple case of civil dispute but intention of the petitioner from very NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4830/2013 ORDER DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined beginning is to infringe the right of the complainant, who received the title, interest of the property by way of decree of the Civil Suit.
4. The inherent powers of the Court under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. has to be exercised sparingly when the case is not made out for the offences alleged on reading of the complaint itself or in case where such complaint is filed by way of abuse of process.
5.

In the case referred by learned advocate Mr.Gandhi of Dr.Lakshman Vs. The State of Karnataka &
Ors reported in (2019) 9 SCC, 677, the Hon'ble Apex Court has referred to the case of MOU executed for land property and objects were issued which were pleaded to be as a security for the amount of advance.

Here, in this case, the allegation is that in spite of knowing the fact, the matter was settled in the Lok-Adalat and the decree was drawn in favour of the complainant and the property was entrusted and necessary consideration was again paid to the daughters of Bhikhabhai Chhitabhai, and the land was given in ownership.
Inspite of that fact, sale deed was executed and thereafter again, it was resold to an Advocate.

Fraudulent and dishonest intention at the time of commission of offence is the primary consideration of the complaint while invoking Sections 406 and 420 the IPC and the fact as alleged in the complaint suggests that the petitioner has the knowledge of the decree and the ownership right granted to the complainant.
Hence, this Court is of the view that the petitioner has not made any case for quashment of the FIR.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4830/2013 ORDER DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined 7.
The present application is hereby rejected.
Notice is discharged.
Interim relief, if any, stands vacated.
